findings.classification: automatic follow-up dequeue can lose a queued prompt when the send fails
findings.trigger: A queued follow-up is automatically drained after the active turn ends; the socket becomes non-open (or write throws) before the message is accepted by the local transport.
findings.impact: sendNextFollowUp destructively removes the first queued item before sendPrompt proves the write succeeded. On failure, the TUI marks a generic retry status but neither restores that prompt to its per-session queue nor to the composer, so the queued user text is no longer actionable.
findings.counterevidence: Direct composer failure intentionally preserves the draft and is source-tested. Normal queued follow-up send, edit/restore and per-session queue retention are also source-tested; the uncovered case is specifically automatic dequeue followed by synchronous send failure.
findings.smallest_alternative: Peek the next follow-up and commit dequeue only after send succeeds, or reinsert/restore the exact prompt on send failure.

findings.classification: context-panel completion can overwrite a newly switched session
findings.trigger: The user opens /context for session A, then switches to session B before A's fetchSessionContext request completes.
findings.impact: The late A response unconditionally updates contextTokens, lastUsage, title and the context panel after the await, so B can temporarily show A's context summary/token usage. This is same-client cross-session UI state contamination, not a server authorization bypass.
findings.counterevidence: Session metadata, context estimate, history pagination and branch/session loads elsewhere in the same app carry chat or generation fences; existing /context source tests cover only the same-session success path.
findings.smallest_alternative: Capture chat identity plus a request generation at openContext start and ignore completion/error UI commits when either no longer matches.

final_discussion_questions.question: Should queued follow-ups use explicit delivery/acknowledgement state so automatic dequeue is committed only after local transport admission succeeds?
Should all TUI session-scoped HTTP/discovery reads share one chat/request-generation fence, including /context and connection-rotated runtime controls?
Should the persistent Desktop gateway lifetime remain independent of TUI/adapter detach, with stop authority only in explicit Desktop lifecycle commands as implemented today?
What idempotency/replay contract should TUI WebUI mutations use across disconnects, especially recovery continue/dismiss where server application can be ambiguous?
Which exact private-state and origin guarantees are mandatory for future Desktop platforms if the current Fedora private socket, loopback gateway and Tauri origin restrictions are generalized?

entry_rules.bounded_body_reads: Each entry needs repository, commit, tree, path, Git blob, SHA256, exact inclusive line ranges or bounded symbols, purpose and evidence origin. Empty files need an explicit empty marker. Only supplied body evidence receives body credit; no all-branch certification.
entry_rules.caller_context_reads: Record exact bodies/ranges actually read for caller tracing; keep context distinct from the assigned primary review disposition.
entry_rules.search_only: Record actual search operands, roots and resulting paths; unconfirmed operands and mere symbol hits receive no body-read credit.
entry_rules.test_source_reads: Record source ranges read as text and relevance; no test execution or automatic primary-body credit.
entry_rules.support_reads: Record config, documentation, assets, dependency or history material with its own pin/path/ranges and purpose; no primary-body credit.
entry_rules.justified_exclusions: Identify each path or bounded branch, reason, compatibility consequence and accepting authority; absence is not silently excluded.
entry_rules.material_unread_gaps: Account for each assigned target without sufficient supplied body evidence and each material unread branch/caller; retain next action and impact on provisional judgement.
entry_rules.reference_mechanisms_or_nonapplicability: Use pinned DSH/Codex implementation evidence or an explicit module-specific reason for nonapplicability; no parity assumption.
entry_rules.findings: Retain ID, requirement, source/call chain, trigger, impact, confidence/uncertainty, smallest alternative, consequences and dependencies.
entry_rules.counts: Report unique primary assignments separately from body paths/ranges, context/search/test/support counts, exclusions and gaps. Shared reads and P01 add no denominator.
entry_rules.acceptance: Only supplied coordinator evidence may populate coordinator_check, integrated_review or git_checkpoint. Template nulls convey no acceptance.

additional_observations.note: Desktop adapter/Tauri use strict bounded protocol frames, loopback-only endpoints, per-launch auth secret, exact gateway ID/version/capability validation, private runtime/socket ownership and remote-origin command denial.
Tauri keeps uncertain start/stop disposition explicit, binds lifecycle replies to captured handles and refuses quit while stop cannot be confirmed.

GatewayRuntime release_desktop_lease intentionally preserves a persistent gateway and stop_desktop verifies process birth/listener identity. TUI close-before-open also rechecks closedByClient. The earlier U01 shorthand orphan concern is retired as no finding.

RuntimeControls can reuse an in-flight controlsPromise across apiUrl/apiToken rotation, and command/mention discovery has similar lower-impact stale completion exposure. Workspace access remains gateway-authoritative, so this is retained unpromoted.
TUI recovery mutations are rejected rather than replayed after socket close; app state keeps actions retryable, but ambiguous server-application/idempotency semantics belong with E02.
Transcript/diff/LaTeX paths are bounded and turn-scoped; PTY scripts validate restoration semantics; release packaging checks runtime-license closure and ships source/relinking material.
